        return all(seq[i] < seq[i + 1] for i in range(len(seq) - 1))

    def is_matrix_increasing(matrix):
        for row in matrix:

                return False
        for col_idx in range(m):

            if not is_strictly_increasing(column):
                return False
        return True

        # Check each position (i, j) to see if we can swap to fix the increasing order

                if is_matrix_increasing(rows_a) and is_matrix_increasing(rows_b):

                # Revert the swap to try another swap or move to the next position
                rows_a[i][j], cols_a[j][i] = cols_a[j][i], rows_a[i][j]
                rows_b[i][j], cols_b[j][i] = cols_b[j][i], rows_b[i][j]

    # Check if a given sequence is strictly increasing
    def is_strictly_increasing(seq):
        return all(seq[i] < seq[i + 1] for i in range(len(seq) - 1))
    
    # Check if both rows in a matrix are strictly increasing
    def are_rows_strictly_increasing(matrix):
        return all(is_strictly_increasing(row) for row in matrix)
    
    # Check if both columns in a matrix are strictly increasing
    def are_columns_strictly_increasing(matrix):
        return all(is_strictly_increasing([matrix[i][j] for i in range(n)]) for j in range(m))
    
    # Check if both matrices are initially strictly increasing
    if not (are_rows_strictly_increasing(matrix_a) and
            are_columns_strictly_increasing(matrix_a) and
            are_rows_strictly_increasing(matrix_b) and
            are_columns_strictly_increasing(matrix_b)):
        return "Impossible"
    
    # Try to make both matrices increasing by swapping elements
    # We will check pairs of elements from the same position in both matrices
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(m):
            # Swap elements
            matrix_a[i][j], matrix_b[i][j] = matrix_b[i][j], matrix_a[i][j]
            
            # Check if after the swap, both matrices are strictly increasing
            if (are_rows_strictly_increasing(matrix_a) and
                are_columns_strictly_increasing(matrix_a) and
                are_rows_strictly_increasing(matrix_b) and
                are_columns_strictly_increasing(matrix_b)):
                return "Possible"
            
            # Swap back to the original configuration
            matrix_a[i][j], matrix_b[i][j] = matrix_b[i][j], matrix_a[i][j]
    
    return "Impossible"

def is_possible_to_make_increasing(n, m, matrix_a, matrix_b):
    # Check if a given sequence is strictly increasing
    def is_strictly_increasing(seq):
        return all(x < y for x, y in zip(seq, seq[1:]))

    # Check if all rows of a matrix are strictly increasing
    def all_rows_increasing(matrix):
        return all(is_strictly_increasing(row) for row in matrix)

    # Check if all columns of a matrix are strictly increasing
    def all_columns_increasing(matrix):
        return all(is_strictly_increasing([matrix[i][j] for i in range(n)]) for j in range(m))

    # Check if both the given matrices are initially strictly increasing
    if not all_rows_increasing(matrix_a) or not all_columns_increasing(matrix_a):
        return "Impossible"
    if not all_rows_increasing(matrix_b) or not all_columns_increasing(matrix_b):
        return "Impossible"

    # Verify if swapping any two elements between corresponding positions in matrices can help
    # to make both matrices strictly increasing
    def can_fix():
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(m):
                # Create temporary matrices with the swap
                temp_a = [row[:] for row in matrix_a]
                temp_b = [row[:] for row in matrix_b]
                temp_a[i][j], temp_b[i][j] = matrix_b[i][j], matrix_a[i][j]
                
                # Check if both matrices are strictly increasing after the swap
                if all_rows_increasing(temp_a) and all_columns_increasing(temp_a) and \
                   all_rows_increasing(temp_b) and all_columns_increasing(temp_b):
                    return True
        return False

    # If a swap can fix the matrices, return "Possible", otherwise "Impossible"
    return "Possible" if can_fix() else "Impossible"
